channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: India: Tactical duration opportunity on rates – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Sherilyn Chew notes that renewed geopolitical risk has lifted yields across Asia, but sees Indian G-Secs as offering a tactical opportunity. She argues the India sell-off is mainly macro repricing, with domestic fundamentals and structural demand intact.

item.title: Gold firms but lacks momentum amid US-Iran tensions, hawkish Fed bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) firms on Thursday as a mildly softer US Dollar (USD) and a modest pullback in US Treasury yields help the precious metal recover some ground after three consecutive days of losses.

item.title: Fed: Hawkish minutes keep upside rate risks – ING
item.description: ING strategists Michiel Tukker and Benjamin Schroeder note that the Federal Reserve’s June minutes confirmed a more hawkish stance despite an unchanged policy rate.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed minutes flag supply-driven inflation risks – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists highlight that the June Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) Minutes showed rising concern over inflation risks, even as the United States (US) labor market remains stable.

item.title: Japanese Yen gains modestly, remains near multi-decade lows
item.description: USD/JPY trades slightly lower on Thursday as a mildly softer US Dollar (USD) lends support to the Japanese Yen (JPY). At the time of writing, the pair is trading around 162.45, hovering near 40-year highs.

item.title: Czech Koruna: CNB alignment may weigh CZK against Euro – BNY
item.description: Geoff Yu at BNY Mellon highlights that Czech National Bank policy expectations have risen alongside the ECB, yet the Czech Koruna is sliding on a nominal effective basis.

item.title: Confirmed: ECB Accounts reveal growing concerns over upside inflation risks
item.description: The European Central Bank (ECB) released the accounts of its latest monetary policy meeting on Thursday, revealing growing concern among policymakers over persistent inflationary risks.

item.title: Fed: Divergent inflation paths shape rate outlook – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Jan Groen notes that the June Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) minutes confirmed a hawkish hold, with the Summary of Economic Projections (SEP) showing an even split between members favoring unchanged or lower rates and those preferring hikes.

item.title: US Initial Jobless Claims dropped to 215K last week
item.description: According to a report from the US Department of Labour (DOL) released on Thursday, the number of US citizens submitting new applications for unemployment insurance shrank to 215K for the week ending July 4.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: Rate support constrained by Oil drag – OCBC
item.description: Christopher Wong highlights that the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) has strengthened after a hawkish Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) rate hike, but higher Oil prices are capping gains.

item.title: Aluminium: Price outlook shifts lower as market rebalances – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists have downgraded its Aluminium price outlook as supply recovers and demand softens. They now expect Aluminium to average $3,378/t in 2026 and $3,281/t in 2027, projecting smaller deficits and a move toward market balance while still ruling out a major rout.

item.title: Brent: Supply recovery meets weak China demand – ING
item.description: ING’s Warren Patterson notes that Oil prices fell after the US–Iran Memorandum of Understanding allowed Persian Gulf supply to recover faster than expected, while demand lagged.

item.title: Euro: Sideways trading outlook against US Dollar – Rabobank
item.description: RaboResearch Global Economics & Markets discusses how Euro sentiment has cooled after optimism around Germany’s debt brake, with political risks and structural headwinds weighing on the currency.

item.title: Oil: Strait of Hormuz risks keep prices supported – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights that Oil is back in focus as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz nears a standstill and ceasefire risks rise. iFlow data show energy equities flows stabilizing after June profit-taking, with valuations and under-ownership becoming more attractive.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Pound consolidates after hitting fresh all-time highs at 218.00
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) is pulling lower against the Japanese Yen (JPY) on Thursday, after hitting a fresh all-time high at 218.01 earlier on the day.

item.title: Euro falls back as US Dollar recovers early losses
item.description: The Euro (EUR) retreats to near 1.1425 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Thursday. The major currency pair falls back as the US Dollar claws back a majority of its early losses, with the appeal of safe-haven assets improving in the wake of renewed geopolitical risks.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed minutes flag supply-driven inflation risks – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists highlight that the June Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) Minutes showed rising concern over inflation risks, even as the United States (US) labor market remains stable.

item.title: Mexican Peso: Gains seen limited against US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister observes that markets expect substantial tightening by Banxico over the next year, but he questions whether conditions justify 75 basis points of hikes.

item.title: CEE FX: Forint longs face geopolitical test – ING
item.description: ING’s Frantisek Taborsky reports that the National Bank of Poland kept a neutral stance, with elevated uncertainty from Middle East tensions and CPI projections above expectations. US–Iran headlines triggered a sell-off in CEE rates and FX, with EUR/HUF jumping 1.2%.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar extends rebound after RBNZ rate hike, US-Iran tensions cap gains
item.description: NZD/USD advances on Thursday and trades around 0.5730 at the time of writing, up 0.56% on the day.

item.title: British Pound hits fresh three-week highs past 1.3400 as US Dollar pulls back
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) appreciates against the US Dollar (USD) for the second consecutive day on Thursday, to hit fresh three–week highs right above 1.3400.

item.title: Indian Rupee regains ground despite higher oil prices
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) opens higher against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday. The USD/INR pair drops to near 95.40 as the US Dollar ticks lower; however, the outlook of the pair remains bullish as renewed Middle East hostilities have boosted oil prices.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: Recoveries likely be capped as 20-day EMA slopes lower
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) trades 0.8% higher to near $4,110 during the European trading session on Thursday. The precious metal gains as the US Dollar (USD) is down despite a slight improvement in expectations that the next monetary policy move by the Federal Reserve (Fed) will be on the upside.

item.title: Silver Price Forecasts: XAG/USD picks up above $59.00 as US Dollar softens
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) is trimming losses on Thursday, and hitting session highs just above $59.00 after bouncing from $57.22 lows on Wednesday.

item.title: WTI slips below $74 after recent rally, Middle East tensions limit the downside
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) trades lower on Thursday and hovers around $73.10 at the time of writing, down 1.95% on the day as investors take profits following two consecutive days of strong gains.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Slips despite yield support – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Philip Wee notes the US Dollar Index (DXY) slipped from 101.28 to 101 late in the US session, even as the US Treasury 2Y yield rose and crude Oil stayed supported by Middle East tensions.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Thursday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $59.17 per troy ounce, up 1.45% from the $58.32 it cost on Wednesday.

item.title: Euro advances against Canadian Dollar on strong German trade, weak oil
item.description: EUR/CAD gains ground after two days of losses, trading around 1.6210 during the European hours on Thursday. The currency cross remains stronger following stronger-than-expected trade data from Germany.

item.title: Euro: ECB hawkish repricing with bond selloff – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank Research’s Early Morning Reid notes that European assets are sensitive to the renewed energy shock. Market pricing for ECB hikes by December rose sharply, implying a chance of three hikes this year after June’s move.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Fed hawks supported by energy spike – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner notes that higher Oil prices and Gulf tensions have driven a bigger reaction in rates than in FX, with Brent near $80 supporting Fed hawks. The US Dollar (USD) is expected to stay firm versus low-yielders, while carry trades in Emerging Markets (EM) have been unwound.
